text.p: Copper prices lurched lower again overnight through technical levels on the London Metal Exchange as bearish sentiment continued to dominate.
Aluminium prices fell in sympathy and nickel was weak also.
Gold prices dropped on NYMEX to fresh two-month lows on still absent industrial demand before support kicked in.
Crude oil prices jumped as fears of a widening Iraqi conflict sparked a late session rally following a day of big price swings.
Iraq issued a veiled threat to Kuwait and the United States weighed in with a warning it would defend Kuwait, adding it had sent another carrier to the gulf.
Wheat prices fell again on confirmation from the USDA of higher supply. Sugar closed just weaker after climbing from early lows on trade short-covering.
The CRB Index closed down 0.13 points at 247.09.
Copper prices lurched lower in Thursday afternoon LME trading with Wednesday's break below $1,900 followed by fresh technical sales and liquidation.
Traders said the market was hit by bearish sentiment, given the speed at which prices have fallen from early September peaks of $2,165, and further losses are on the cards.

Final three months business was at $1,852 a tonne, just $1.50 above the low, but a hefty $63 down from Wednesday's kerb. Copper prices lurched lower on Thursday in late inter-office activity but edged up off a new two-month low at $1,840.

COMEX copper plunged lower for the second day running, ending with some of the losses pared, in fragile technical health and funds continuing to sell their long futures positions, brokers and analysts said.December settled 1.25 cents off at 85.90 cents.
The pressure on the red metal in London followed losses in aluminium on Wednesday and resulted in negative sentiment spreading through most other metals.

Aluminium notched another two-year low, hitting $1,429 at one point. Levels under $1,430 sparked some covering and prices closed the kerb at $1,435, still down $3.50 from Wednesday. Another stock increase is expected on Friday, traders said.
Nickel followed the trend and continued to re-trace from Wednesday's 2-1/2 month peaks.
New York precious metals prices slid to fresh two month lows Thursday before some shortcovering helped provide some support near the close.
"There's a dearth of investor demand, and industrial usage has not yet picked up after the usual summer lull," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"Renewed talk about IMF gold sales may be disconcerting to retail investors, but the plan has been discounted into prices by the trade for months," he said.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $382.45/382.95, compared to the London afternoon fix at $382.10, which was the lowest fix since July 9 this year.

NYMEX crude oil prices closed higher Thursday as fears of bullish overnight news on the Iraqi conflict sparked a late session rally following a day of big price swings, traders said. October crude closed up 25 cents at $25.00 a barrel after rising as high as $25.30 and falling as low as $24.26.
"It was a roller-coaster day, and everybody's waiting to see what's going to go on with Iraq," said a trader.

The United States said it was readying F-117A stealth bombers and B-52 long-range bombers in retaliation against Iraq after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. jets. Iraq warned Kuwait not to permit U.S. planes to use it as an attack base.
The U.S. also said it was sending a carrier to the gulf and warned it would defend Kuwait against Iraqi attacks.
Confirmation Wednesday by USDA that world wheat stocks were increasing again pressured CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
The government's U.S. and world supply/demand reports Wednesday continued to weigh on the wheat market, they said.

USDA this week said world wheat ending stocks for the 1996-97 marketing year would total 117.43 million tonnes, up from 108.68 million tonnes forecast by the government in August. Export concerns also hit prices with competition from Canada, Australia, Argentina and the EU a driving force in the wheat futures market.
Wheat futures closed six cents per bushel lower to 2-3/4 higher, with September down six at $4.38.
CSCE world sugar futures closed a moderately traded session weaker, climbing from early lows on trade shortcovering in October and producer buying in March, dealers said.

Options activity also supported the market above support seen at 11.85 cents a lb in October as trade buying of October calls at the 11.50 strike price prompted the locals who sold the call options to buy futures against the calls, a dealer said.
Liquidation of October and March contracts, and speculators rolling long positions into March ahead of the October contract's end-of-the-month expiry, also kept prices weaker.
LCE white sugar futures ended the day mixed ahead of Friday's expiry of the October contract. The spot month ended up 80 cents a tonne at $346.40.
